source_acquisition.search_note: The CSV row is no_public_source_found and the local corpus/visual_sources directory is absent. The PDF links only to the paper and dataset assets, not author plotting code. gh read-only inspection confirmed google-research-datasets/GSM-IC is an archived dataset-only repository with four data/README files and no plot/table/LaTeX source. Exact-title and arXiv-id repo searches returned no repository; voidful/icml2026 is an ICML metadata mirror and seshurajup/myclew contains a reproduction-log pointer, neither a validated visual source. No source file is therefore recorded as source_exact.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figures 2–3 use five categorical tab10-like strategy colors plus a black threshold; Figure 1 uses pastel semantic stage/card fills and red/green/blue/orange hand-drawn emphasis. Tables stay monochrome and encode hierarchy with bold, underline, italic, arrows, and booktabs rules.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figure 1 is mixed (embedded raster panels/icons with PDF text/vector elements); Figures 2–3 are vector paths; all tables are vector text and rules. No public source establishes exact plotting parameters.
paper_style.style_consistency: The two frontier plots share log-x, linear-y, threshold/crossing line grammar, palette, and legend placement. Tables 1/2/4 share metric columns and grouping; Tables 8/9 extend that schema with split-level spanners. Figure 1 is stylistically more illustrative but keeps stage colors aligned with the method narrative.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. Overview. Top: We compare intrinsic dimensionality across reasoning strategies and evaluate how well it predicts generalization performance (c.f. Section 3). Middle (Green): To compute the intrinsic dimension of a reasoning strategy, we sweep varying LoRA parameter counts d and identify the minimum d_int at which training accuracy crosses a common threshold τ (described in Section 2.3). This Pareto frontier for a single strategy is shown across all strategies simultaneously in Figure 2. Right: We find a strong inverse correlation between intrinsic dimensionality and generalization performance (Section 4).

color.semantic_mapping: Pastel fills distinguish strategy/data cards; green marks the ID method, orange the evaluation, blue the finding, and red the motivating question/selected result.

encodings.x: trainable parameters/intrinsic dimension in embedded charts
encodings.y: training accuracy and Overall accuracy in embedded charts
encodings.line: solid frontier, dotted threshold/relationship guides, and directional arrows
encodings.text: direct text labels, example outputs, and findings

figures.data_and_statistics: Representative examples only: No CoT 7.18%, Short CoT 32.63%, and Exec PoT 46.15%; the green inset illustrates a roughly 63% crossing at d_int ≈ 1.5M and the blue inset sketches Overall accuracy versus intrinsic dimension. It is not the full 14-strategy dataset and displays no uncertainty or split-level aggregation.
figures.evidence_relation: Connects the §2.2 LoRA interface and §2.3 d_int definition to §3 training/evaluation and §4 generalization; the single-strategy crossing explicitly points forward to Figure 2.
design_strengths: A single scan exposes the strategy → adapter sweep → intrinsic dimension → OOD evaluation chain.
Concrete same-question examples, arrows, and direct labels make the method interface understandable before the detailed plots.
Semantic stage colors separate data, method, evaluation, and finding without requiring a separate legend.
design_weaknesses: The conceptual, representative numeric, and quantitative panels are dense and small at print size.
Hand-drawn hatching and pastel differences are not robust in grayscale; the embedded mini-plots lack independent axis/legend/uncertainty explanations.
Representative values can be mistaken for the complete result and the pipeline styling may imply stronger causal direction than the strategy-level correlations establish.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a three-stage overview with concrete input examples, an operational capacity/crossing inset, and an outcome scatter; bind each arrow to a short definition or finding.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2. Visualization of intrinsic dimension computation for Gemma-3 4B showing select reasoning strategies. We plot the Pareto frontier of monotonic training accuracy versus trainable parameters (log scale). The dashed line indicates the threshold (τ = 63.0%); intrinsic dimension is the parameter count where each curve first crosses this threshold (vertical dotted lines). Strategies crossing earlier have lower intrinsic dimensionality and tend to yield higher overall performance (cf. Table 1).

color.semantic_mapping: Five colored lines identify the selected reasoning strategies; black identifies the 63.0% threshold.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: below the plot, centered in two rows

encodings.x: intrinsic dimension / trainable parameters on a logarithmic axis
encodings.color: strategy identity via tab10-like categorical colors
encodings.shape: small circular sweep marks where visible
encodings.line: solid Pareto frontiers; same-color dotted crossing guides; black dashed threshold

figures.data_and_statistics: Each displayed curve is the monotonic Pareto frontier from a LoRA rank/target-module sweep. The common threshold is τ=63.0%; d_int is the first parameter count at which a curve crosses it. The selected curves include Exec PoT, Gemma 27B CoT, No CoT, Short CoT, and Very Short CoT; no seed dispersion or uncertainty band is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Operationalizes the §2.3 d_int formula and supports §4.1/§4.4 claims about Exec PoT crossing at 1.49M and less effective strategies crossing later; Table 1 supplies the complete strategy-level performance comparison.
design_strengths: Log-scaled x makes several orders of trainable capacity visible in one panel.
The common horizontal threshold and color-matched vertical crossing guides make the operational definition auditable.
Vector paths and a caption that defines crossing allow the visual to be cross-checked against Table 1.
design_weaknesses: Only five selected strategies are drawn, so the figure is not a complete inventory of the 14 strategy sweeps.
The five colored curves plus six reference guides become crowded at the high-capacity end and the below-plot legend increases lookup cost.
No training seeds, run variability, confidence bands, or failed configurations are visible.
figures.reusable_pattern: For capacity sweeps, use a log-x monotonic frontier, one shared capability threshold, same-color crossing guides, and a caption that defines the crossing estimand.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3. Visualization of intrinsic dimension computation for Gemma-3 1B showing select reasoning strategies. We plot the Pareto frontier of monotonic training accuracy versus trainable parameters (log scale). The dashed line indicates the threshold (τ = 24.3%); intrinsic dimension is the parameter count where each curve first crosses this threshold (vertical dotted lines).

color.semantic_mapping: Five colored lines identify selected 1B strategies; black identifies the 24.3% threshold.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: below the plot, centered in two rows

encodings.x: intrinsic dimension / trainable parameters on a logarithmic axis
encodings.color: strategy identity via the same five-color categorical palette as Figure 2
encodings.shape: none apparent in the rendered step curves
encodings.line: solid Pareto frontiers; same-color dotted crossing guides; black dashed threshold

figures.data_and_statistics: The 1B selected curves are Critical CoT, Exec PoT, Gemma 27B CoT, Short CoT, and Very Short CoT. The common threshold is τ=24.3%; vertical dotted lines mark the first parameter count crossing. Values are training-curve frontiers, not accuracy uncertainty intervals.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix A.2 provides this 1B analogue; §4.2 and §4.4 compare it with Figure 2 to discuss model-scale interaction and delayed Very Short CoT crossing. It reproduces the method grammar rather than adding a new estimator.
design_strengths: Reusing Figure 2 axes, colors, line styles, and crossing definition makes the cross-scale comparison direct.
Log x preserves the capacity-order story despite the lower 1B threshold.
The appendix placement keeps the main headline focused while retaining the visual evidence for reproduction.
design_weaknesses: Only selected strategies are shown and no training variability or uncertainty is encoded.
The threshold changes from 63.0% in Figure 2 to 24.3%, so absolute crossings are not directly comparable without reading the caption and Tables 1–2.
Small ticks and a bottom legend remain hard to parse when reduced.
figures.reusable_pattern: Copy the main capacity-frontier grammar into an appendix cross-scale panel, changing only model and threshold while keeping colors and line semantics fixed.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1. Performance of Gemma-3 4B across reasoning strategies. ID: Accuracy on GSM8K Test. OOD: Geometric mean of 5 stress test sets (GSM-Symbolic, GSM-IC, GSM-Hard). Overall: Geometric mean across all 6 splits (refer to Table 8 for a breakdown of accuracy across splits). Spearman correlations are computed between each metric and overall accuracy; for metrics marked with ↓, +ve correlations indicate that lower values successfully predict higher accuracy. Note: † denotes statistical significance (p < 0.01).

tables.uncertainty: No intervals, SD/SE, or seed dispersion are reported. The dagger marks p<0.01 for the strategy-level Intrinsic Dimensionality and Token PPL correlations; OOD and Overall are geometric aggregates.
tables.data_and_statistics: Gemma-3 4B; 14 strategy rows report GSM8K ID accuracy, five-stress-test OOD geometric mean, six-split Overall geometric mean, intrinsic dimension (M), sequence KL, token PPL, and length. The summary row gives Spearman correlations 0.93†, -0.17, 0.82†, and 0.31 across strategies.
tables.evidence_relation: §4.1 headline comparison and Figure 2 validation; Table 8 expands the OOD/Overall aggregates, while the common threshold and LoRA sweep come from §2.3.
design_strengths: Combines performance, capacity, and competing proxy metrics in one decision surface.
Direction arrows plus bold/underline best and second-best marks work without color.
The appendix pointer makes the aggregate numbers traceable.
design_weaknesses: Geometric means compress stress-split heterogeneity; the table offers no run-level uncertainty or paired significance.
Four different metric scales and 14 strategies create a dense lookup task.
The caption says five stress tests but names only three, so the denominator must be recovered from the body/appendix.
tables.reusable_pattern: Make the main result table include outcome, capacity, alternative metrics, direction arrows, and a strategy-level summary row, then link to split-level detail.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2. Performance of Gemma-3 1B across reasoning strategies. ID: Accuracy on GSM8K Test. OOD: Geometric mean of 5 stress test sets (GSM-Symbolic, GSM-IC, GSM-Hard). Overall: Geometric mean across all 6 splits (refer to Table 9 for a breakdown of accuracy across splits). Spearman correlations are computed between each metric and overall accuracy; for metrics marked with ↓, +ve correlations indicate that lower values successfully predict higher accuracy. Note: † denotes statistical significance (p < 0.05).

tables.uncertainty: No intervals, SD/SE, or seed dispersion are reported. The dagger marks p<0.05 for the 1B strategy-level Intrinsic Dimensionality and Token PPL correlations.
tables.data_and_statistics: Gemma-3 1B with the same 14 strategy rows and metric schema as Table 1. The summary correlations are ID 0.75†, KL -0.18, token PPL 0.63†, and length 0.24; Executed PoT is 1.03M/11.00/11.76 for ID/OOD/Overall.
tables.evidence_relation: §4.2 cross-model replication; Figure 3 supplies the matching 1B frontier and Table 9 expands the split aggregates. The different 1B threshold limits raw ID comparisons with 4B.
design_strengths: Exact column and group structure makes the model-scale replication easy to read.
Outcome and proxy metrics remain adjacent, preserving the prediction comparison.
Monochrome emphasis gives best/second-best hierarchy without fragile color.
design_weaknesses: The 1B threshold is 24.3% rather than 63.0%, so absolute ID values are not an unconditional scale comparison.
No seed/run variation or paired test is shown, and OOD heterogeneity remains aggregated.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use an isomorphic companion table for a second model, changing only model-specific values and significance note.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3. Robustness to threshold selection for computing intrinsic dimension using epoch 1 training accuracy at 70%, 80%, and 90% of the maximum achieved by any strategy, and 90% of validation accuracy by any strategy.

tables.uncertainty: No confidence intervals, repeated-training variation, or per-strategy threshold crossings are given; the rows are deterministic threshold-selection conditions.
tables.data_and_statistics: Four threshold choices are compared: 90%, 80%, and 70% of maximum epoch-1 train accuracy and 90% of validation accuracy. Columns report Spearman correlations for 1B (0.75, 0.72, 0.73, 0.73) and 4B (0.93, 0.94, 0.93, 0.94).
tables.evidence_relation: §4.3 robustness check for the common-threshold choice; it qualifies the ID correlations in Tables 1–2 rather than introducing a new result metric.
design_strengths: Compactly juxtaposes model sizes and the full tested threshold range.
Minimal booktabs layout keeps the robustness question legible.
design_weaknesses: Only the summary correlation is shown, not the changed strategy ordering or curve crossings.
No uncertainty or seed sensitivity is visible.
tables.reusable_pattern: Arrange predeclared threshold alternatives by row and model sizes by column, with the estimand and tested range in the caption.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4. Performance on Reasoning Gym tasks for Gemma-3 4B across algorithmic and cognitive reasoning categories. ID: Geometric mean of accuracies across three tasks, OOD: geometric mean over out-of-distribution splits with hard configuration and held-out tasks Overall: denotes the geometric mean across all evaluation splits. Spearman correlations are computed between each metric and overall accuracy across the four strategies. For metrics marked with ↓, +ve correlations indicate lower values predict higher accuracy.

tables.uncertainty: No p-values, intervals, seed dispersion, or task-level uncertainty are reported; correlations are computed over only four strategies within each category.
tables.data_and_statistics: Reasoning Gym Gemma-3 4B results are split into Algorithmic and Cognitive groups. Each group has four strategy rows plus a Spearman summary, with ID/OOD/Overall geometric means and intrinsic dimension, KL, token PPL, and length. Algorithmic Exec PoT is 0.74M/73.21 Overall; Cognitive No CoT is 0.40M/49.82 Overall.
tables.evidence_relation: §4.5 cross-domain result; Appendix C and Table 6 provide task configurations. Separate groups preserve the cognitive counterpattern while connecting to the same metric schema as Tables 1–2.
design_strengths: Independent row groups keep domain heterogeneity and the No CoT cognitive counterexample visible.
The shared columns permit direct comparison with GSM8K tables.
Best/second-best typography works in black and white.
design_weaknesses: Four strategies per group makes Spearman values sensitive to a single ordering.
Task and split geometric means hide within-category variation, and the caption is tightly packed.
tables.reusable_pattern: For domain transfer, retain a common metric schema but compute and display one row group and summary correlation per domain.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5. Effect of training data correctness on intrinsic dimensionality and generalization (Gemma-3 4B). Mixed sets consist of 50% correct and 50% incorrect reasoning chains.

tables.uncertainty: No seed, interval, or instance-level decomposition is reported. The 50% condition is a mixed training-set intervention, not an uncertainty distribution.
tables.data_and_statistics: Short CoT and Gemma 27B CoT are each shown at 100% correct versus a 50% correct/50% incorrect mixture. Short CoT changes from Overall 32.63 and d_int 3.92M to 20.61 and 2729.64M; Gemma 27B changes from 42.04/2.05M to 29.24/257.18M.
tables.evidence_relation: §4.4 correctness mechanism/failure ablation; it contrasts with clean strategy rows in Tables 1–2 and motivates the contradictory-signal explanation.
design_strengths: Puts correctness condition, generalization, and capacity in one compact comparison.
The large direction and magnitude change is immediately visible without color.
design_weaknesses: Only two strategies are tested and the mixture changes supervision content as well as correctness, so the causal path is not isolated.
No uncertainty or per-example error analysis is available.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a clean-data anchor and one mechanism perturbation, reporting the outcome and capacity proxy side by side.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6. Algorithmic and cognitive reasoning task ask configurations for easy (ID), hard OOD, and held-out OOD splits of Reasoning Gym tasks evaluated in Table 4.

tables.uncertainty: No errors or intervals apply; the table lists deterministic configuration ranges. Split caps and fixed/different seeds are stated in surrounding Appendix C text, not in cells.
tables.data_and_statistics: Ten task rows cover six Cognitive/Algorithmic tasks with Easy and Hard configurations plus four unseen held-out tasks (needle_haystack, modulo_grid, letter_counting, count_primes). Ranges, ≤, and n∈ encode configuration difficulty rather than statistical estimates.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix C reproduction interface for Table 4; the table makes the ID/hard-OOD/held-out-OOD task boundaries explicit.
design_strengths: Configuration ranges and held-out task types are visible in one matrix.
Monospaced task identifiers are easy to copy and align with the prose.
design_weaknesses: Held-out rows have no Hard Config value and use a Default configuration in Easy Config; sample counts and seeds are absent from the table.
Mixed range notation increases scanning cost.
tables.reusable_pattern: Place task family, easy/hard ranges, and unseen held-out tasks in one configuration matrix before reporting transfer results.

tables.label: Table 7

caption.text: Table 7. Spearman rank correlations with generalization performance (Gemma-3 4B) for PPL-based metrics and intrinsic dimensionality. LongPPL variants use the original α, β values from Fang et al. (2025).

tables.uncertainty: No p-values, intervals, or seed-level dispersion are reported; the upward arrow only defines the preferred correlation direction.
tables.data_and_statistics: Gemma-3 4B strategy-level Spearman correlations are LongPPL K=64 0.60, LongPPL K=256 0.62, Token Perplexity 0.82, and Intrinsic Dimensionality (ours) 0.93. LongPPL uses the original α, β settings from Fang et al. (2025).
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix D metric replacement ablation; it directly revisits the token-PPL 0.82 and ID 0.93 values in Table 1.
design_strengths: Very small table with a single metric column makes the baseline hierarchy immediate.
Caption identifies model, metric family, and inherited LongPPL settings.
design_weaknesses: Only one model and strategy cohort are used, with no statistical uncertainty or cost column.
The table reports correlations but not the underlying strategy points.
tables.reusable_pattern: Compare a proposed metric with close baseline replacements in one ranked correlation column, leaving implementation details in the appendix text.

tables.label: Table 8

caption.text: Table 8. Detailed Performance of Gemma-3 4B across test splits. Symb: GSM-Symbolic; P1/P2: Symbolic Perturbations; IC: GSM-IC; Hard: GSM-Hard. OOD: Geometric Mean of the 5 stress tests. Overall: Geometric Mean of all 6 splits.

tables.uncertainty: No run-level uncertainty, intervals, seed dispersion, or failure counts are displayed; each cell is split accuracy and OOD/Overall are geometric aggregates.
tables.data_and_statistics: Gemma-3 4B per-strategy accuracy is expanded over GSM8K ID, GSM-Symbolic Main (Symb), P1, P2, GSM-IC (IC), GSM-Hard, and OOD/Overall aggregates. The 14 rows and eight numeric measures recover Table 1; for example Exec PoT is 62.77/63.64/48.24/18.80/63.30/42.15/43.40/46.15.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix F reproduces and decomposes Table 1; the two-level ID/OOD/Aggregates header exposes what the headline geometric means hide.
design_strengths: Split names, aggregates, and strategy groups remain in one auditable table.
Two-level spanners make the evaluation denominator explicit.
Typography preserves the best/second-best hierarchy used in the main table.
design_weaknesses: High information density and small text make cross-split comparisons costly.
No uncertainty or per-split sample count is reported, and the aggregate still requires mental recomputation.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a multilevel header to place each raw split beside the aggregate used in the headline table.

tables.label: Table 9

caption.text: Table 9. Detailed Performance of Gemma-3 1B across test splits. Symb: GSM-Symbolic; P1/P2: Symbolic Perturbations; IC: GSM-IC; Hard: GSM-Hard. OOD: Geometric Mean of the 5 stress tests. Overall: Geometric Mean of all 6 splits.

tables.uncertainty: No run-level uncertainty, intervals, seed dispersion, or failure counts are displayed; cells are split accuracy and OOD/Overall is a geometric aggregate.
tables.data_and_statistics: Gemma-3 1B uses the same 14 strategy rows and split columns as Table 8. Exec PoT is 20.24/18.54/8.80/1.96/38.28/10.69/11.00/11.76; High Review Ratio is 22.60/14.30/5.84/2.20/66.28/5.08/9.00/10.57.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix F reproduces and decomposes Table 2; isomorphism with Table 8 supports cross-scale split-level checking, while Figures 2–3 clarify that thresholds differ.
design_strengths: Identical structure to Table 8 makes 1B/4B split comparison straightforward.
Raw stress-test columns prevent complete dependence on the aggregate headline.
design_weaknesses: Two dense tables share one page and remain small; no uncertainty is supplied.
Different model thresholds mean that ID comparisons still require the frontier figures and main captions.
tables.reusable_pattern: Keep split-level companion tables isomorphic across model sizes so aggregates can be traced without a new decoding scheme.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 introduces strategy→LoRA sweep→intrinsic dimension→generalization; Figure 2 operationalizes the 4B crossing; Tables 1–2 report main and cross-model comparisons; Table 3 tests threshold robustness; Table 4 transfers across domains and preserves a cognitive counterexample; Table 5 exposes correctness failure; Figure 3 and Tables 6–9 supply scale, task, metric-ablation, and split-level reproduction.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Every object begins with a numbered caption. Figures 1–3 state setup and frontier/crossing encoding; Figures 1–2 also state the inverse-correlation finding. Tables 1/2/4/8/9 define abbreviations, aggregates, and direction arrows; Tables 3/5/6/7 primarily define settings or comparisons. There is no common uncertainty-caption convention because no object displays intervals or error bars.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Main comparison tables use strategy plus ID/OOD/Overall and metric-proxy columns, with downward/upward arrows for preferred directions. Group labels are italic, best/second-best values use bold/underline, and split tables use two-level ID/OOD/Aggregates spanners. Horizontal rules follow booktabs without vertical borders.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: The LoRA/d_int definition in §2.2–§2.3 becomes the crossing grammar in Figures 1–3; Tables 1–2 quantify the predictor, Table 3 varies its threshold, Table 4 tests domain transfer, Table 5 tests correctness, and Table 7 replaces the PPL baseline. These support a strategy-level correlation narrative, not an independent causal proof.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Table 1 points to Table 8, Table 2 to Table 9, Table 4 to Table 6, and Figure 2 has the 1B analogue Figure 3. Appendix D/Table 7 expands the metric comparison; Appendix F exposes split heterogeneity. Appendix E is qualitative text/Code examples rather than additional labeled figures.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: The paper uses Roman/Computer Modern text for captions and tables, with embedded DejaVu Sans/Computer Modern in the vector plots and Sen-like sans in Figure 1. Table sizes and hierarchy are stable; plot labels are smaller than body text but repeated consistently between Figures 2 and 3.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Figures 2 and 3 reuse the same blue/orange/green/red/purple strategy palette and black threshold. Figure 1 uses a separate pastel stage palette, with semantic green/orange/blue stage boxes that echo the method/result sequence; tables intentionally avoid color.

most_reusable_patterns: A fixed-model, common-threshold capacity sweep rendered as a log-x Pareto frontier with same-color crossing guides.
A main table that puts outcome, capacity, alternative metrics, directions, and a strategy-level summary in one decision surface.
Isomorphic cross-model and raw-split appendix tables that make geometric aggregates auditable.
Domain-transfer tables that retain separate row groups and expose counterexamples rather than averaging them away.
highest_value_objects: Figure 2: operationalizes d_int as a visible threshold crossing.
Table 1: combines the full 4B strategy comparison with ID/PPL/KL/length correlations.
Figure 1: makes the strategy-to-generalization interface legible before details.
Table 5: puts correctness, generalization, and capacity into a direct mechanism/failure comparison.
failure_patterns: High-density Figure 1 mixes concept, representative values, and miniature charts; decorative hatching and pastel color degrade at small/grayscale reproduction.
Figures 2–3 show selected curves only and omit training-run uncertainty.
Geometric means in Tables 1/2/4/8/9 compress stress/task heterogeneity, while all objects omit seed dispersion or intervals.
Absolute ID across 1B and 4B is constrained by different capability thresholds, requiring careful cross-reference.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: A high-information strategy→capacity→generalization overview is followed by shared log-scale Pareto crossing plots and monochrome booktabs comparison/ablation tables, with cross-scale, cross-domain, and split-level appendix objects closing the audit trail.
